'Has ketch value' is functional..why: A made-up relation (has_ketch_value, fictional, no property tags before the insert) given a property and applied to real instances. 'Ketch' is an ordinary English word (a sailing boat) and not a mathematical term, so only the phrase 'ketch value' is new: a model has no default reading of it with this property, and an unrecorded relation has no property to contradict. Paired with mathematics-replace-0011.

notes: RBox expansion, functionality, paired with mathematics-replace-0011 (which makes 'has derivative' not functional). The made-up relation 'has ketch value' relates functions to numbers; nothing in the name suggests a unique value, and a model cannot read uniqueness off the real function names (cos x, e^x). The new property is functional: the direct question asks whether two different ketch values are possible (new answer no). Every original answer is null. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the first instance asks whether the two values must coincide (yes), the second whether they could differ (no); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. The instance values are letters, so no arithmetic can give the conclusion. The propositional negation asks the opposite of the edit ('can have two different ketch values'), since a functional property has no short 'is not' form; its answer is no after the edit. The conjunction and disjunction state the edit as 'has at most one ketch value'. Side facts (a right angle) are copied from the paired revision. Near unrelated is a real many-valued slot (square roots), whose answer yes would turn to no if functionality leaked to other relations. hops counts the instance facts in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1).
